_comment: SOURCE OF TRUTH for the Animation Studio roadmap rendered at /animation-studio/roadmap. Hand-maintained: update task `status` (planned, in-progress, done) as work lands in the UnysonPlus-Animation-Studio repository, and `extensionVersion` to the Studio version.

milestones.title: Phase 1 · Foundations
milestones.goal: The parts everything else stands on: the project, the scene file, the player that plays it, the responsive stage and the route to the live site. At the end of this phase a hand-written scene file plays correctly on the subdomain.

tasks.title: Project scaffold
tasks.detail: A GitHub repository with a React + TypeScript editor built by Vite, and a separate plain-JavaScript player package. Both build to static files.

tasks.title: Scene file, version 1
tasks.detail: The JSON format with tracks, clips, preset settings, keyframes, assets and breakpoints, plus a schema that validates it and a version number so later formats can upgrade older files.

tasks.title: Player runtime
tasks.detail: Reads a scene file and builds one GSAP timeline. Seekable and repeatable: no unseeded randomness and no real-time physics, so any frame can be shown exactly.

tasks.title: Responsive stage
tasks.detail: An aspect ratio per breakpoint, the three height modes (**ratio**, **ratio capped to the window**, **fill the window**), sizes in CSS container units, and a safe-area guide.

tasks.title: Deploy to the subdomain
tasks.detail: A GitHub Action builds the editor and publishes it to GitHub Pages at `animation-studio.unysonplus.com` (HTTPS) on every push to main.

milestones.title: Phase 2 · Editor
milestones.goal: The working studio: a canvas, a timeline and a first preset library, enough to build a hero animation by hand from start to finish.

tasks.title: Canvas and layers
tasks.detail: Text, image and shape layers on the stage; click to select, drag to move with snapping to the centre and the safe area, resize with handles, and double-click to edit text in place.

tasks.title: Multiple selection, Align and Distribute
tasks.detail: Select several layers with Shift or Ctrl + click, a dragged box or Ctrl+A; move them together; align their edges or centres to each other, the stage or the safe area; distribute them by edge, centre or equal gaps; and lock layers so they stay put.

tasks.title: Groups
tasks.detail: Group layers (Ctrl+G) to manage big scenes: a group has a timeline of its own, opens with a double-click (breadcrumb, everything else dimmed, Escape steps back), moves in time as one by dragging its bar, and takes presets as a whole. Ungrouping keeps every layer where and when it was.

tasks.title: Timeline
tasks.detail: Tracks and clips; drag, trim and move clips; a playhead with frame-accurate scrubbing; zoom; play, pause and loop.

tasks.title: Inspector
tasks.detail: Edit the selected clip's settings (text, image, colours, duration, easing), with per-breakpoint overrides for position, size and type size.

tasks.title: Preset library, first set
tasks.detail: 22 presets in a drag-and-drop panel, each with a live preview on hover: text (rise, slam, stretch, scramble, typewriter, blur, flip, tracking), reveal and exit (fade, wipe, iris, slide, grow), move and scale (pop, zoom, spin, keyframes) and emphasis (wave, pulse, shake, float, recolour).

tasks.title: Measured eases and better defaults
tasks.detail: Twelve named eases measured from professional motion pieces (Soft land, Snap and settle, Pop over, Leave…), each with what it is for. Exits default to an accelerating curve, staggered text gets a natural uneven rhythm, and the preset defaults follow measured timing.

tasks.title: Check scene
tasks.detail: A Check tab that reviews the scene as you work: text that leaves before it can be read, text too small on a screen size, text off the stage or on other text, clips fighting over a layer, long stretches with nothing moving. One-click fixes, Apply all, and Fix with AI.

tasks.title: Undo, redo and saving
tasks.detail: Full undo and redo (a drag is one step), the working scene saved in the browser automatically, and project files (`.scene.json`) to download and reopen.

tasks.title: Playback modes
tasks.detail: Play on load, play when scrolled into view, and loop or play once.

milestones.title: Phase 3 · Export
milestones.goal: Get a finished scene out of the Studio and onto a website.

tasks.title: Standalone HTML export
tasks.detail: One HTML file that contains the scene and the player and runs anywhere.

tasks.title: Embed snippet
tasks.detail: Copy-and-paste embed code from the Export window: the scene inline plus the player, loaded from its permanent versioned address. Works in any page that accepts HTML, such as a Custom HTML block in WordPress.

tasks.title: Images and fonts in exports
tasks.detail: Uploaded images travel inside the scene. Web fonts can be embedded in the downloaded page (Latin character sets packed in, others left linked), so it works offline.

tasks.title: Player versioning
tasks.detail: Downloaded pages carry their own copy of the player; embeds load a published player version that never changes. The build refuses to publish a changed player under an existing version number.

tasks.title: Accessibility
tasks.detail: Respect reduced-motion settings, keep text as real text, and give decorative layers the right hidden roles.

milestones.title: Phase 4 · Unyson+ integration
milestones.goal: Put Studio scenes into Unyson+ pages and share one preset library with the Animation Engine.

tasks.title: Page-builder element
tasks.detail: The **Studio Scene** element (Animation Engine → Studio Scene) plays a scene inside a Unyson+ page with the bundled player: paste the scene file or the embed code, and override the height mode, header height, start and loop for that placement.

tasks.title: Open in Studio
tasks.detail: **Open in Animation Studio** opens the Studio with the element's scene; **Save to page** sends the edited scene straight back into the element. Each side only accepts messages from the other.

tasks.title: Shared preset library
tasks.detail: Presets usable both in the Studio and in the [Animation Engine](/animation-engine), so an effect is built once.

milestones.title: Phase 5 · AI
milestones.goal: Describe an animation in words and get an editable scene, using the AI Dev Kit on the user's own computer.

tasks.title: Studio-to-kit connection
tasks.detail: The Studio reaches the AI Dev Kit on the user's computer (`localhost:8787`). The kit only answers the Studio's own pages. Browsers ask once before a website may reach apps on the device; the Studio explains the prompt and what to do if it was refused.

tasks.title: Prompt to scene
tasks.detail: The AI tab turns a request into a scene file built only from the preset catalogue (sent with each request, so the kit never goes stale). The result is validated; an invalid answer gets one automatic repair round. It lands on the timeline as ordinary clips, one undo step.

tasks.title: Edit by prompt
tasks.detail: "Change this scene" or "Change the selected layers": the AI returns the whole scene with only the asked-for change, keeping every other layer and id, and re-checks the layout at every screen size so bigger text never overlaps or leaves the safe area.

tasks.title: AI assist panel
tasks.detail: A floating ✦ AI assist button over the stage opens a chat with the AI Dev Kit: who is answering, scope chips (this scene, the selected layers, a new scene), starter ideas, and for every answer one undo step, "Go back to before this" and a Check scene count. The Studio sends its motion rules with each request.

tasks.title: Custom code clip
tasks.detail: An escape hatch for effects no preset covers: a clip that runs your own GSAP code. It runs only where the page allows it (the Studio, your own exports, and WordPress pages by authors trusted with unfiltered HTML), a failing clip never stops the scene, and the AI never writes one.

tasks.title: AI Dev Kit hub
tasks.detail: The kit's dashboard opens on a Home page with a card per job (Site Converter, AI Assistant, Animation Studio): whether each is ready, when it last called the kit and from which site, plus the AI in use. Retitled Unyson+ AI Dev Kit.

milestones.title: Phase 6 · 3D and finer control
milestones.goal: 3D objects on the timeline, and hand-keyframed motion for anything the presets don't cover.

tasks.title: 3D clips
tasks.detail: 3D layers drawn by three.js: extruded 3D text, shapes, extruded SVG logos and glTF/GLB models, with matte to chrome finishes and studio lighting. Spin 3D, Tumble in, Orbit and Camera push presets; every frame drawn from the timeline, so 3D seeks, loops and scroll-links. three.js loads only for scenes with a 3D layer.

tasks.title: Keyframe and curve editor
tasks.detail: Keyframes clips with a track per property (move, scale, rotation, opacity, blur), an ease per keyframe and custom curves drawn with two handles (overshoot and anticipation allowed). Add keyframes at the playhead, drag diamonds on the timeline, or drag the layer on the stage to set its position keyframe.

tasks.title: Scroll-linked playback
tasks.detail: Starts: As the page scrolls. The scroll position is the playhead, forwards and back. Pin while playing holds the stage below the header for a set number of screens; smoothing glides the playhead. Built without a scroll plugin, in the Studio, the exports and the Studio Scene element (with a Scroll length option), plus a Try scrolling test page.

tasks.title: More presets
tasks.detail: 35 presets in six groups, including Count up, Soft wipe, Blinds, Turn, Sheen, Drift, Gradient flow, Particles and the 3D set (Tumble in, Spin 3D, Orbit, Camera push), plus transitions between groups (Crossfade, Push, Zoom through, Soft wipe, Blinds, Iris, 3D turn) applied from the group Inspector.

milestones.title: Phase 7 · Later
milestones.goal: Useful additions once the core works, none of which change the scene file.

tasks.title: Video export
tasks.detail: Export → Video renders MP4 (H.264) or WebM (VP9) at Full HD, HD, 4K, vertical or square, 24 to 60 fps. The AI Dev Kit (1.12.34) draws the scene frame by frame in headless Chrome and encodes it with ffmpeg, so every frame is exact, 3D included.

tasks.title: Share links
tasks.detail: Export → Share link puts the whole scene, compressed, inside the link: anyone who opens it gets their own copy in the Studio. No account, no server and no storage; custom code clips are removed from shared scenes.

tasks.title: Save to Google Drive
tasks.detail: Projects on any computer without our own server: people sign in with Google and their scenes are saved to their own Drive. Planned if people ask for cross-device projects.

tasks.title: Accounts and cloud projects (only if needed)
tasks.detail: If real accounts are ever needed (a project library, short links, embeds that update in place), they run on a free cloud tier, separate from the website hosting, with uploads on object storage and embeds still served from GitHub Pages.

tasks.title: Click-to-advance presentations
tasks.detail: Timeline markers and Playback → Advance: On click. The scene stops at each marker until a click, a tap or the arrow keys, with a pulsing hint; full screen is a presenter mode; without motion it jumps slide to slide.

milestones.title: Phase 8 · Sound and voice
milestones.goal: Voice-overs, music and sound effects, and scenes made from a voice-over with AI.

tasks.title: Audio track
tasks.detail: Voice-overs, music and sound effects on the timeline with waveforms, trimming, volume and fades, played in step with the animation. Scenes with sound start muted on pages (a Tap for sound button), and video exports mix the sound in.

tasks.title: Built-in sound effects
tasks.detail: Effects generated in code (pop, click, whoosh, rise, impact, sparkle, typing): no files, no licences. A Sound option on any clip adds the matching effect on the frame the motion lands.

tasks.title: Styles (scene presets)
tasks.detail: Ready looks the AI and the user can build from: palette, type, motion personality, pacing and a sound palette, each with a reference scene. Save your own scenes as styles; a brand kit (logo, colours, fonts) on top.

tasks.title: Transcription in the AI Dev Kit
tasks.detail: Whisper speech-to-text on your own computer, with the time of every word, plus how it is said: emphasis, pauses, pace and energy.

tasks.title: Make a scene from a voice-over
tasks.detail: Upload a voice-over and, with AI connected, get a scene timed to the words: key phrases as text, presets that match the delivery, transitions between ideas and automatic sound effects, in the style you pick.

tasks.title: Studio tools for AI apps (MCP)
tasks.detail: The AI Dev Kit offers the Studio as tools to AI apps such as Claude Desktop, so a scene can be made or changed from a conversation.
